In some parts of Africa and Asia, female genital mutilation (FGM), also known as female circumcision, is still practiced.
Many people erroneously believe that FGM is important for good hygiene or to preserve women's virginity (driven by cultural and religious beliefs), and to ensure that they remain marriageable.
